source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade / Downgrade DCSCM-CPLD firmware by Web when system is off
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade DCSCM-CPLD firmware through web UI
(Need to do AC cycle after flash complete).

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

original_test_intent: Have an engineer upgrade and downgrade the DCSCM-CPLD through the BMC WebUI while the host begins off, then perform the mandatory AC cycle and prove both CPLD activation and restoration of the management-module and host paths affected by DCSCM logic.
original_method: The Master path is attended WebUI programming followed by AC removal/restoration. The linked raw-IPMI version script is a supporting readback only after its field is mapped to the exact DCSCM-CPLD; it cannot prove WebUI operation or management-path recovery.
manual_activity: A qualified engineer operates the WebUI image selection/confirmation and observes terminal programming status, then authorizes or performs the controlled AC cycle. Because DCSCM may participate in management routing, the operator must keep an independent console/recovery path outside the normal DCSCM-dependent route.
required_inputs: DCSCM board identity, CPLD instance/revision and current/target versions
signed upgrade/downgrade images, hashes and supported order
vendor WebUI programming, safe-to-remove-power and activation instructions
approved AC control method, off/on dwell, count and management-path effects
independent console/rescue route plus expected DCSCM, BMC network and host health
safety_requirements: Bind the image to the exact DCSCM board and CPLD; do not substitute FPGA, HIB-CPLD or a different management-module image.
Do not remove AC until the WebUI reports the vendor-defined terminal and safe-to-cycle state.
Capture BMC addresses, routes and alternate access before programming because DCSCM activation may interrupt the normal management path.
Verify post-AC DCSCM identity, BMC network reachability and host boot independently; neither a WebUI banner nor a raw version string is sufficient.
Preserve the first programming, power, network, console and SEL failure and never reflash or repeat the AC cycle automatically.
agent_execution_scope: Before the manual core, capture DCSCM/CPLD identity, BMC network routes, alternate console, SEL and host baselines and organize immutable image evidence.
After the engineer's AC cycle, verify authoritative DCSCM version, management address/routes/services, BMC health, SEL, console POST and OS health through independent paths.
Analyze supplied WebUI/power evidence and report gaps without operating controls or assigning PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
engineer_actions: Approve and perform each DCSCM-CPLD WebUI transition and exact AC-cycle hand-off.
Judge both active firmware and restored management/host behavior, then issue separate verdicts for upgrade and downgrade.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It keeps the named component and AC step, but browser automation violates ED-25 and its clean-single-reset phrase does not establish the source's full AC transition or management recovery.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor WebUI manually, wait for the documented safe-power gate, perform the approved AC cycle, and validate DCSCM plus management connectivity using an independent recovery path.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: DCSCM-CPLD target, WebUI method, initial host-off state, mandatory AC cycle, linked script and 5/30-minute values remain source evidence.

modernized_recommendation.status: ATTENDED DCSCM-CPLD UPDATE WITH INDEPENDENT MANAGEMENT RECOVERY
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind one signed image to the exact DCSCM-CPLD, capture engineer-owned WebUI terminal status, execute a controlled AC activation after safe-to-cycle, and verify CPLD version, management networking/services, BMC health and host boot through a non-DCSCM-dependent path.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: DCSCM-based systems whose vendor WebUI supports CPLD programming and requires AC activation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record DCSCM hardware/CPLD image, BMC/WebUI/browser, network configuration, readback decoder, console and AC-controller revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor DCSCM-CPLD programming, management recovery, AC activation and rescue documentation plus project power SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds board-instance binding, safe-power evidence, alternate access and management-service verification while retaining the source WebUI action.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An alternate approved updater may prove a project transition but not the WebUI path; CPLD version equality alone cannot show the management plane recovered.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Approved DCSCM image, management and AC plan.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: If ordinary BMC access traverses DCSCM-controlled logic, the recovery channel must not depend solely on that same path.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may select another tool or AC controller, but must retain original WebUI versus actual method, reason, approval, equivalent checkpoints and uncovered WebUI coverage. The target remains DCSCM-CPLD and cannot be generalized to FPGA.
expected_evidence: approved DCSCM board/CPLD/version/image matrix with hashes and signatures
host-off/BMC-standby baseline including management addresses/routes/services and independent console
engineer-owned WebUI selection, confirmation, progress, terminal status and safe-to-cycle evidence
AC controller, dwell and timestamped power telemetry
post-AC authoritative DCSCM version plus BMC network/services, SEL, console POST and OS health
independent recovery readiness and separate engineer verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target DCSCM-CPLD through WebUI with a required AC cycle. Exact images, management paths and power timing are project inputs; DeepSeek's clean-single-reset addition is excluded.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The DCSCM-CPLD target, WebUI method and AC activation are clear. Missing project artifacts are readiness inputs; engineer-operated UI and power actions make the complete case MANUAL ONLY, not permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes PARTIAL to MANUAL ONLY, preserves DCSCM/host-off/AC scope, and rejects unapproved browser control plus reset conflation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its management/power recovery gates but removes permanent BLOCKED because the project can supply exact artifacts and timing.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Independently confirms manual ownership and strengthens DCSCM-specific alternate-path evidence rather than relying on the archived conclusion.

review_improvement: Makes management-path loss and independent recovery first-class acceptance concerns instead of treating DCSCM programming as only an image version change.
independent_technical_reasoning: DCSCM-CPLD may control or mediate management functions that are needed during recovery, so the proof path must remain usable even if normal BMC networking does not return. The source lifecycle is coherent after project binding, but WebUI acceptance and AC control are human-owned; MANUAL ONLY therefore preserves actual coverage without converting missing inputs into BLOCKED.
